cases.scenario: A small request has one clear output and one write surface.
invariants: No subagents are created.
Work proceeds as one unit.

cases.scenario: The user asks only for a plan for a multi-part task.
invariants: Returns an orchestration plan.
Creates no subagents, worktrees, branches, or mutations.

cases.scenario: Two proposed units both need an unsettled shared interface.
invariants: Work remains serial until the interface is resolved, or a shared foundation is accepted first.
Concurrent writes to the shared interface do not occur.

cases.scenario: Two units have fixed inputs, distinct owners, no write conflicts, and separate acceptance checks.
invariants: The units may be scheduled in the same parallel wave.
Each unit retains isolated ownership and verification evidence.

cases.scenario: Applicable Codex project instructions explicitly constrain an executor configuration.
invariants: The applicable AGENTS.md instruction chain controls each field it specifies.
Any unspecified field follows the generic runtime policy.

cases.scenario: Applicable Claude Code project instructions explicitly constrain an executor configuration.
invariants: The applicable CLAUDE.md instruction sources control each field they specify.
Any unspecified field follows the generic runtime policy.

cases.scenario: Applicable policy requires an executor setting that the current host does not expose or allow.
invariants: The explicit requirement is not silently replaced.
The unit inherits an allowed parent setting, runs serially, or reports the limitation.

cases.scenario: A shared foundation changes after dependent units submitted results.
invariants: Affected dependent results are marked stale.
Affected work is revalidated or reissued against the new foundation snapshot.

cases.scenario: An independent validator starts its first pass after integration.
invariants: Initial context excludes implementer self-assessments and expected conclusions.
Validation reports evidence and reproducible findings rather than a supplied conclusion.

cases.scenario: Code work is dispatched to isolated worktrees.
invariants: Each worker writes only in its assigned worktree.
The assigned worktree is the worker current directory.
The integration branch owns final integration.

cases.scenario: A delegated unit or Validator considers creating another worker.
invariants: Nested delegation does not occur.
Only the top-level coordinator launches, steers, waits for, or stops executors.

cases.scenario: Codex uses a full-history fork for a unit.
invariants: The executor inherits the parent runtime configuration.
The spawn does not request an explicit model or reasoning override.

cases.scenario: Claude Code delegates a unit to a subagent with a separate context.
invariants: The handoff includes the complete unit contract and authoritative inputs.
The unit does not rely on hidden parent conversation history.

cases.scenario: Claude Code native worktree isolation is proposed for a writing unit.
invariants: The actual worktree baseline is verified against the accepted integration commit.
An unsuitable baseline causes manual isolation or serial execution instead.

cases.scenario: The current Agent Skills host has no verified delegated-agent capability.
invariants: No parallel execution is claimed.
The coordinator executes serially or returns a plan while preserving the same acceptance gates.
